metadata.title: ORCHID-Assemblages: assessed phase assemblages of binary systems
metadata.description:
ORCHID-Assemblages: assessed phase assemblages of binary systems: one record per named phase field of the expert-drawn (assessed) binary phase diagrams compiled in H. Okamoto's Desk Handbook (ASM International, 2010): the thermodynamic coordinate (T, x, P) of a point deep inside the field and the phase assemblage present there, with phase-registry ids, coordinate uncertainty from the axis calibration, naming basis, confidence and review state, a cross-check against the calculated SGTE diagrams, and citations (original evaluation first, the handbook as compilation). Evidence class assessed_phase_diagram. Part of the ORCHID data release v2026.10.

What

  • 23,129 points from 2,178 diagrams (centroid 21,616, pole of inaccessibility 1,513); 11,961 two-phase points with a drawing-based tie_line block (low credence).
  • ESPEI ZPF datasets, one per diagram: default (two-phase compositions null with a __HYPERPLANE__ at the point) and a variant with tie-line endpoints. The files pass ESPEI dataset-format checks; this establishes format compatibility and does not validate the scientific correctness of all assemblages or their locations.
  • JSONL, CSV, Parquet, exclusions with reasons, SCHEMA.md.

Limitations

  • Version 1, machine-extracted: fields named by deterministic rules, model readers, an adjudicator and partial expert review (basis and review state per record).
  • Drawing-based tie lines and interior points are soft constraints with recorded naming basis and review state.
  • No page images, crops or handbook text are distributed.

Licence

CC BY 4.0. The stated licence covers the ORCHID-produced content in this deposit; upstream data and software retain their documented terms and attribution requirements, and no publisher pages, handbook drawings or restricted TDB source files are included.

How to cite

R. Arróyave, J. Saal, D. Shin, ORCHID-Assemblages: assessed phase assemblages of binary systems (version 2026.10; Version 1, machine-extracted), Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23735996

Part of: R. Arróyave, J. Saal, D. Shin, ORCHID data: umbrella record of the ORCHID datasets (version 2026.10; Version 1, machine-extracted), Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23736065

Cite each diagram's original evaluation and the Okamoto handbook as the compilation.

Software and data citations

These credits describe the ORCHID project and its examples. Cite the papers and software used in your analysis, together with the ORCHID release and original source of each observation. The list does not imply that every dataset was generated with every package. Preserve the versions and commit hashes recorded by each example; a repository link is not a reproducibility pin. Materials Project and OQMD energies retain separate references.

  • pycalphad: Thermodynamic calculations and phase equilibria. R. Otis and Z.-K. Liu (2017), pycalphad: CALPHAD-based Computational Thermodynamics in Python (10.5334/jors.140). Repository.
  • ESPEI: Thermodynamic parameter fitting and uncertainty quantification. B. Bocklund et al. (2019), ESPEI for efficient thermodynamic database development, modification, and uncertainty quantification: application to Cu–Mg (10.1557/mrc.2019.59). Repository.
  • PhaseForge: MLIP-informed CALPHAD construction in the examples. S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Machine learning potentials for alloys: a detailed workflow to predict phase diagrams and benchmark accuracy (10.1038/s41524-025-01814-z). Repository; archived software.
  • PhaseForge+: Construction and experimental tuning of CALPHAD models in the examples; repository name PhaseForgePlus. C. Kunselman, S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Construction and Tuning of CALPHAD Models Using Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and Experimental Data: A Case Study of the Pt–W System (10.1007/s11669-025-01222-2). Repository; archived software.
  • Materials Project: DFT structures and energies; repository link is the API client, not the database itself. A. Jain et al. (2013), Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation (10.1063/1.4812323). Repository; data resource.
  • OQMD: DFT structures and energies; qmpy is the supporting software. J. E. Saal et al. (2013), Materials Design and Discovery with High-Throughput Density Functional Theory: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD) (10.1007/s11837-013-0755-4); S. Kirklin et al. (2015), The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD): assessing the accuracy of DFT formation energies (10.1038/npjcompumats.2015.10). Repository; data resource.
